title: Build the static planning-read and `<Suspense>` confinement check, with failing fixtures
statement: Implement the analysis that runs without executing the application and reports file and line for a planning-content filesystem read performed anywhere other than the reader, and for a read site not enclosed by a `<Suspense>` boundary. Ship fixtures containing both violations and prove the check fails on each.
notes: ⚠️ Split from TSK-0006 on 2026-08-27. This half needs the reader to exist, because the rule it enforces is 'reads go through the reader' — there is nothing to be outside of until there is one. ⚠️ ACC-0024 is satisfied by the PAIR with TSK-0006, and it holds for each half separately: a check nobody has seen fail is a check nobody has seen. ⚠️ Both halves land before any view work. Built afterwards they would arrive to a codebase already full of violations, and the pressure would be to weaken the rule rather than fix the code. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28. Four detectors, six fixtures, eleven tests, and three defects found before anything was trusted — two in the fixtures (import paths that climbed out of the app directory, so the ALLOWED case reported clean because nothing resolved) and one in the analyser (two template-literal regexes that lost a backslash level, leaving a detector unable to fire at all). ⚠️ THE SUSPENSE DETECTORS HAVE NOTHING TO CHECK IN THE REAL APPLICATION YET — the lint reports `0 reader consumer(s)`, because no view imports the reader until TSK-0007. That is stated rather than left for someone to discover: today they are proven by fixtures and by temporary real-code violations, and they begin covering real code with the first view.
